name: L7
label: Sub Pop
lede: Four women from Los Angeles who named themselves after slang for square, wrote riffs heavy enough to move furniture, and got a wrestler, a Prodigy cover and a British TV scandal out of it.

eras.title: Squares from Echo Park
eras.text: Donita Sparks and Suzi Gardner start a band in Los Angeles, go through a bassist-and-drummer shuffle, and land a debut on Epitaph. It takes until a drummer named Dee Plakas arrives for the lineup to stick.

years.h: [[Donita Sparks|03b6f1e2-70b5-46c9-b290-193d31289fee]] and [[Suzi Gardner|8be0f670-d96e-4a9c-bd52-4feb2310ba9e]] start L7 in Los Angeles
years.p: Both came out of the Echo Park art-punk scene. The name is slang for square, picked so nobody could file them under all-female novelty.
years.xp:
Wikipedia dates the band to 1985 and says Sparks and Gardner met through the LA Weekly crowd in 1984. Gardner has described first hearing Sparks's music as one of the happiest days of her life.

On the name, Sparks has said the band deliberately avoided a title that flagged their gender. She has also said they had no female role models growing up, and that letters from young women who picked up instruments because of L7 mean a lot to them.

years.h: [[Jennifer Finch|add94f0b-8aba-4534-bda4-b1c6796b2d63]] and drummer Roy Koutsky make it a four-piece
years.p: Finch on bass, Koutsky on drums. This is the lineup that made the first record.

years.h: L7: debut LP on Epitaph
years.p: Fast, straightforward punk, made before the sludge set in. Koutsky left afterward.

years.h: Dee Plakas takes the drum stool and stays
years.p: She follows Anne Anderson, whose only studio trace is a cover of "Yummy Yummy Yummy" on SST's compilation The Melting Pot.
years.xp:
Anderson filled in after Koutsky's exit. Plakas's arrival gave L7 the lineup of Sparks, Gardner, Finch and Plakas that recorded everything through 1994.

Chicago Tribune critic Greg Kot later singled Plakas out as the band's secret weapon.

eras.title: Nine songs, Sub Pop, and a phone call from Slash
eras.text: Sub Pop gets a single and a mini-album from L7 in the space of a year, and by the end of 1991 the band has a major-label deal and a benefit concert with Nirvana on its résumé.

years.h: Shove b/w Packin' a Rod: the Sub Pop Singles Club 7-inch
years.p: L7's first release for Sub Pop is a single, and the label made it a Single of the Month.

years.h: Smell the Magic: nine songs, four stars from Rolling Stone
years.p: The Sub Pop record that made L7 a name outside LA. Rolling Stone praised the twin guitars of Sparks and Gardner, racing "down the highway to hell."
years.xp: Sub Pop's own 30th-anniversary edition put all nine songs on one vinyl release for the first time, remastered. The record now sits at No. 24 on Ugly Things magazine's list of the 40 best punk albums, per Wikipedia.

years.h: L7 plays Olympia's International Pop Underground Convention, freshly signed to a major
years.p: The indie-rock summit's lone band with major-label ties: Slash Records, a London Records subsidiary, had just signed them.
years.xp: Wikipedia notes L7 was the only act at the convention with major-label representation. For a band that Sub Pop had put on the map a year earlier, the move to Slash was the first step out of the underground.

years.cap: L7 at Le Bataclan, Paris, 2015 · Wikimedia
years.src: Wikipedia: Rock for Choice · Wikipedia: L7 (band)
yt: L7 and Nirvana, Rock for Choice, 10/25/91
years.h: Rock for Choice: L7, Nirvana, Hole and Sister Double Happiness at the Palace
years.p: L7 and LA Weekly editor Sue Cummings start a benefit series for pro-choice legal costs, modeled loosely on Live Aid.
years.xp:
The series raised money for legal expenses tied to anti-abortion violence. It ran independently through 2001, though L7 eventually stepped back to focus on the band.

Later editions brought in Rage Against the Machine, Pearl Jam, Foo Fighters and Ween.

eras.title: Bricks, a tampon, and no trousers
eras.text: Butch Vig produces L7's breakthrough, the radio finds it, and the band spends a year making sure every British tabloid has something to say.

years.h: Bricks Are Heavy: [[Butch Vig|ba30915c-4d33-43c5-8c37-ead0b8061517]] behind the board
years.p: Slash Records' first L7 album has Vig, then fresh off Nevermind, producing. Rolling Stone later named it one of the essential recordings of the 1990s.
years.xp:
"Shitlist" found a second life in wrestling: Wikipedia reports wrestler Jon Moxley used it as entrance music through the mid-2000s, and Brian Pillman used it in ECW in 1996.

Wikipedia also reports the album sold 327,000 copies in the US by June 2000.

years.h: "Pretend We're Dead" gets 13 weeks on US alternative radio
years.p: The single from Bricks Are Heavy peaked at No. 8 on the US Alternative chart, and No. 21 in the UK.

years.h: Reading Festival: mud, feedback and Donita Sparks's tampon
years.p: Sparks pulled a tampon out and threw it into a crowd that had been pelting the stage with mud.
years.xp:
According to Wikipedia, the set was already troubled by technical problems when the mud started flying. Sparks told Guitar World: "The crowd got ugly - they were just being assholes, throwing mud at us the whole set."

The line above is what Sparks shouted as she threw it, as printed by Wikipedia. She has stood by the moment since.

years.cap: L7 at the Emerson Theatre, Indianapolis, circa 1997 · Wikimedia
years.h: Sparks plays "Pretend We're Dead" on The Word without trousers
years.p: Live on British late-night TV, Sparks performed nude from the waist down.
years.xp: Songfacts dates the broadcast to November 20, 1992. Sparks later said the show was already chaotic, with a men's bum contest and hidden-camera stunts, so she "added" her own contribution.

years.h: Rock for Choice Los Angeles: L7 play in beauty-pageant sashes
years.p: Rage Against the Machine headlined a sold-out night with X and Firehose. L7 members performed as beauty contestants, sashes naming cities hit by anti-abortion violence.
years.xp: The previous September 27, the series had filled the Hollywood Palladium with L7, Exene Cervenka, the Red Hot Chili Peppers and Mudhoney.

years.h: Hungry for Stink: "Andres" and a Lollapalooza main stage
years.p: The album reaches No. 117 on the Billboard 200, and the band plays the main stage with the Smashing Pumpkins, Beastie Boys, Nick Cave and the Breeders.

yt: L7 as Camel Lips in Serial Mom
years.h: L7 play a band called Camel Lips in John Waters's Serial Mom
years.p: The band appears in the 1994 film under that pseudonym.

eras.title: The bass chair keeps spinning
eras.text: Finch leaves mid-record, two more bassists come and go, and L7 finish up on their own label. The band still finds room for a Krist Novoselic film and some very pointed banners.

years.h: L7 play Voters for Choice at Constitution Hall with Neil Young and Pearl Jam
years.p: A benefit in Washington, D.C. Wikipedia reports Finch pulled her shirt off for the last song, causing a "slight fuss."

years.h: Finch leaves mid-album; Gail Greenwood takes the bass
years.p: Sparks and Greta Brinkman covered bass on the record until Greenwood, ex-Belly, joined full time.

years.h: The Beauty Process: Triple Platinum
years.p: Their fifth album, the first with Greenwood, arrives alongside a film directed by [[Krist Novoselic|ac05e29f-0561-4445-bb26-5562d2389531]].
years.xp: The pseudo-documentary L7: The Beauty Process, directed by Novoselic, looks at a punk band in a pop market. The band also played Seattle's Bumbershoot that year.

years.h: The Prodigy cover L7's "Fuel My Fire" on The Fat of the Land
years.p: The song came from Hungry for Stink. The Prodigy's version is on their 1997 album.

years.h: Slap-Happy, released on the band's own Wax Tadpole label
years.p: The band flew banners over Lilith Fair and Warped Tour. The one over Warped read "Warped needs more beaver...love, L7."
years.xp: At Lilith Fair at the Rose Bowl in Pasadena on July 17, the banner read "Bored? Tired? Try L7." Greenwood left around this time, replaced by Janis Tanaka, ex-San Francisco's Stone Fox.

years.h: L7 announce an indefinite hiatus
years.p: A note on the band's website said the future of the band was "a bit up in the air." Members scatter into side projects.
years.xp: Sparks and Plakas played in Donita Sparks and the Stellar Moments. Finch formed OtherStarPeople and later the Shocker. Tanaka played bass for Pink; Greenwood played with Bif Naked and reformed Belly.

eras.title: Back, loud, and still on the list
eras.text: L7 return on Facebook, play festivals and finally get a documentary and an album that nobody had to ask major labels for. In 2026 the band loses Jennifer Finch.

years.h: L7 announce they're back
years.p: Sparks posts the news on the band's channels. She'd been rebuilding the fan base on Facebook since 2012, one archival video at a time.
years.xp: The reunion began with archive posts on the band's Facebook page in 2012, and fans reassembled there. The first shows came the following June at Rock am Ring in Germany, then Europe and Riot Fest in the US.

yt: L7: Pretend We're Dead, official trailer
years.h: L7: Pretend We're Dead premieres in Los Angeles
years.p: Sarah Price's Kickstarter-funded documentary interviews the band, Lydia Lunch, Shirley Manson, Krist Novoselic and Butch Vig.
years.xp: The film was nominated for a VO5 NME Award for Best Music Film. Original drummer Roy Koutsky died the same year, on February 15, at 53.

years.h: Detroit (Live): Clutch Cargo's, September 1, 1990
years.p: Easy Action releases a live set from the Smell the Magic tour, 27 years late.

years.h: "Dispatch from Mar-a-Lago" is L7's first new song in 18 years
years.p: Released on Don Giovanni Records. The title is a direct reference to Donald Trump's Florida resort.
years.xp: The follow-up, "I Came Back to Bitch," arrived in February 2018.

years.h: Scatter the Rats: first L7 album in twenty years, on Joan Jett's label
years.p: Blackheart Records issues it after a PledgeMusic campaign. "Burn Baby" is the lead single.
years.xp: Hyperallergic wrote that Sparks and Gardner still "pound out one solid, catchy, immediately identifiable power riff after another."

years.h: Bricks Are Heavy at 30: the whole album, live
years.p: An 18-date tour that plays the album front to back, with a gold-and-black vinyl reissue remastered by Howie Weinberg.

years.h: L7 mark 40 years at the Belasco in Los Angeles
years.p: The band's home-city anniversary show.

years.src: Wikipedia: L7 (band) · Variety: Jennifer Finch · Rolling Stone: Jennifer Finch
years.h: Jennifer Finch dies at 59
years.p: The bassist had been diagnosed with brain cancer and withdrew from L7's Last Hurrah tour, announced in May. Variety and Rolling Stone reported her death.
years.xp: Finch had been in L7 from 1986 to 1996 and again from the 2014 reunion. A GoFundMe for her medical costs and unreleased projects raised nearly $400,000, per Wikipedia.
